result.title: Conformal Sequential Decision Making With Cost and Sublinear Policy Regret Guarantees
result.summary: Automated decision makers, such as AI agents that control robots or network devices, must often satisfy hard cost constraints while maintaining competitive performance. In such settings, a cost measure, such as a safety violation rate, energy consumption, or a distortion level, must stay within a given budget in every episode of operation. Furthermore, a cumulative reward metric, accounting for per-step performance, must stay close to the reward of a meaningful reference policy. We formulate this setup as an episodic sequential decision problem in which the state sequence is arbitrary, and the reward and cost may depend on past actions within the same episode. We propose the online conformal episodic agent (OCEA), a policy that selects one candidate action per episode using a regret-controlled algorithm, and switches to a zero-cost action when the remaining budget cannot absorb the maximum cost of one more round. We prove that OCEA satisfies per-episode cost constraints for every state sequence and for every realization of its internal randomness, while achieving a sublinear expected policy regret with respect to the best action sequence in hindsight from a comparator class satisfying the same per-episode cost constraints. We apply OCEA to risk-averse control and online compression with distortion guarantees.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「每回合须满足硬性成本预算、同时累计回报接近参考策略」的形式化为带任意状态序列的情节式在线决策问题，提出 OCEA：每回合用受 regret 控制的算法选一个候选动作，当剩余预算无法承担再一轮的最大成本时切换到零成本动作，并证明每回合成本约束成立且期望策略 regret 次线性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「剩余预算不足以承担下一轮最大成本即停止/切换」的规则与次线性 regret 分析，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的计算预算分配与停止决策提供可核查的形式化工具；但该工作不涉及视觉或多模态状态，迁移到 latent 推理成本核算的可行性需核查。
